\[
f(x) = -c\, e^{-\alpha \lvert x \rvert} \sin(\omega x)
\]

The formula shows the default parameter values.

where

- \(f\): The derivative filter
- \(\alpha\): How fast the filter decays
- \(\omega\): The frequency of the sine
- \(c\): A scale factor

Canny asked for an edge filter with good detection, good localization and one response per edge. Deriche solved these criteria for a filter of infinite length and found f, a sine under an exponential envelope. Because it is a sum of exponentials, it runs as a recursive filter, two passes along each row or column, in time that does not depend on alpha. The derivative along x is paired with Deriche's smoothing filter along y, and the other way around. At alpha 1 and above, OpenCV's scaling makes a step of h levels peak at h.
